name: Mount Sturgeon
bio_draft: Day walk to the summit of Mount Sturgeon (Wurgarri) above Dunkeld, with views over the plains.

facts.claim: Mt Sturgeon (Wurgarri) Walk is a listed walk in Grampians (Gariwerd) National Park, with its own trailhead
The mount behind Dunkeld, at the southern end of the Grampians; the town was first called Mount Sturgeon
The Grampians Peaks Trail finishes at Dunkeld in the south

access_note: Grampians NP has widespread track closures after 2024/25 damage and roadworks; Parks Victoria's page lists Silverband Falls as still available

name: Mount Piccaninny
bio_draft: Popular leisurely walk to the summit of Mount Piccaninny (Baingga) for views across the south Grampians.

facts.claim: The Piccaninny (Bainggug) Walk is listed in Grampians (Gariwerd) National Park, with a Piccaninny Trailhead; there is also a Piccaninny West Walk

access_note: Grampians NP has widespread track closures after 2024/25 damage and roadworks; Parks Victoria's page lists Silverband Falls as still available

name: Silverband Falls
bio_draft: Falls on the Grampians road reached by a short roadside walk.

facts.claim: Horsetail falls fed by Dairy Creek in Grampians National Park; a narrow band of water tumbles over a small rock face and vanishes into a rocky base
Easy stroll along a fern-laden trail in the Wonderland Range, with birdlife such as yellow robins and wedge-tailed eagles
The creek re-emerges about 50 m west of the falls

access_note: Grampians NP has widespread track closures after 2024/25 damage and roadworks; Parks Victoria's page lists Silverband Falls as still available

name: Halls Gap
bio_draft: Gateway village inside the Grampians, with trail access, a cultural centre, wildlife at dusk and services.

facts.claim: Town in the Fyans Valley at the foot of the Wonderland and Mount William ranges, on Grampians Road beside the national park; about 3 hours from Melbourne
Home to Brambuk, Australia's longest running Aboriginal cultural centre
Halls Gap Zoo is 7 km from town
Grampians Peaks Trail passes through Halls Gap

access_note: Brambuk cultural centre has building upgrades in 2026 (Parks Victoria)

name: Dunkeld
bio_draft: Southern gateway village below Mount Sturgeon, with a heritage trail and walks into the Grampians.

facts.claim: Town at the southern end of Grampians National Park, about 283 km west of Melbourne on the Glenelg Highway
Has a local museum, art gallery, bakery, cafes and a tourist information centre
The Grampians Peaks Trail finishes at Dunkeld

unresolved: heritage trail in bio_draft not verified

name: Stawell
bio_draft: Gold-rush town at the northern gateway to the Grampians, home of the Stawell Gift footrace.

facts.claim: Founded 1853 as Pleasant Creek in the gold rush; one of few Victorian towns with active gold mining, 237 km west-north-west of Melbourne
Famed for the Stawell Gift, a professional footrace begun in 1878
Known as the gateway to Grampians National Park; Bunjil's Shelter rock art is about 10 km south

name: Aradale Lunatic Asylum
bio_draft: Former lunatic asylum at Ararat, a large Victorian-era complex now open for guided tours.

facts.claim: Aradale was a psychiatric hospital in Ararat, begun in 1865 and opened to patients in 1867, closed as an asylum in 1993.
At its height it held up to 1000 patients, and the complex has up to 70 historic buildings.
Guided tours run from the Grano Street entrance, led by Friends of J Ward volunteers.

access_note: Tours on Sundays and Wednesdays at 10am; cancelled on Total Fire Ban days.

name: J Ward
bio_draft: Ararat's old gaol for the criminally insane, open for tours and ghost walks.

facts.claim: J Ward was Ararat County Gaol and later a psychiatric facility for the criminally insane; built 1859-1861.
Volunteer-led guided tours run daily and take 1 to 1.5 hours, and include a museum.
Tours visit the gaol cells, chapel and unmarked graves, with stories of former inmates.

name: Gum San Chinese Heritage Centre
bio_draft: Heritage centre on Chinese gold miners and their story on the Victorian goldfields.

facts.claim: Gum San means Gold Mountain; the centre stands on the site that started Ararat's gold rush.
Life-size scenes tell the story of 19th-century Chinese miners' sea voyage and trek to the Victorian goldfields.
It is managed by volunteers (Friends of Gum San) at 31 Lambert Street, Ararat.

name: Ararat Gallery TAMA
bio_draft: Textile art museum established in 1968, with a collection of contemporary fibre art.

facts.claim: Textile Art Museum Australia, a public gallery in Ararat's late-Victorian Town Hall at Vincent Street and the Western Highway.
Established in 1968, its collection focuses on textile and fibre art from the early 1970s to today.
Includes Olga de Amaral's 'Coraza en dos Colores' (1973), among the most significant formative fibre works in an Australian public collection.

access_note: Exhibition listings say Free Entry, but the Visit page accessibility text says the gallery charges an entry fee; not reconciled.

name: Seppelt Great Western
bio_draft: Historic Seppelt winery at Great Western with underground cellar (drive) tours and tastings.

facts.claim: Seppelt's Great Western winery in the Grampians region dates from the 1860s and produced Australia's first traditional-method sparkling wines and sparkling reds.
Its historic underground Drives cellars are the home of the winery's cellar tours.
Cellar door at 36 Cemetery Road, Great Western.

name: Langi Ghiran State Park
bio_draft: Forested range and walks near Ararat, with a rocky peak and views.

facts.claim: Park 14 km east of Ararat on the Western Highway, covering 2695 ha.
A 1.8 km walking track passes Djab Wurrung rock art and a rock shelter.
The 10 km Easter Creek Track climbs through woodland and granite boulders to views over the mountains and plains.

access_note: Parks Victoria page flags "additional visitor advice"/closure banners; check before visiting. No entry fee listed.

name: Mount Buangor National Park
bio_draft: Forested range near Beaufort with walks, creeks and fern gullies.

facts.claim: Now Mount Buangor National Park, about 5,300 ha combining the former state park with part of Mount Cole State Forest, in forest, fern gullies and escarpments
Mount Buangor is the highest peak in the area and gives wide views over the surrounding countryside
Walks include the Waterfalls Nature Walk, Two Mile Circuit, Middle Creek, Beeripmo and Paradise walks
The park is 60 km west of Ballarat, at Bayindeen, with about 15 km of walking trails

access_note: Reported partial closure after Feb 2024 bushfire: Middle Creek, Ferntree and Bailes campgrounds closed; Ferntree Visitor Area, Ferntree Waterfall walk and Beeripmo walk (Mount Buangor and Grevillea lookouts) open per page. Park was upgraded from state park to national park; spot name may need updating.

name: Hamilton Botanic Gardens
bio_draft: Botanic gardens with a restored rotunda, a small zoo and mature trees.

facts.claim: Site set aside in 1853 and first planted in 1870, among the earliest provincial botanic gardens in Australia
William Guilfoyle, curator of Melbourne Botanic Gardens, designed the layout from 1881 with sweeping lawns, curved paths, lakes and rockeries
Four hectares, National Trust classified in 1990, with eight trees on the Register of Significant Trees
Has fountains, decorative fences and gates, and animal and bird enclosures; on French Street

unresolved: No fee stated on any page read; council public gardens assumed free, not stated

name: Sir Reginald Ansett Transport Museum
bio_draft: Aviation museum on Ansett Australia and its first aircraft, in Hamilton.

facts.claim: Housed in Ansett's first aircraft hangar on the shores of Lake Hamilton, corner of Ballarat Rd and Riley St
Centrepiece is a Fokker Universal aircraft like the one on Ansett's first flight in 1936
Displays include the company's first prospectus, a Boeing 727 wheel and a full set of flight attendant uniforms
Run by an incorporated association

name: Wannon Falls
bio_draft: Falls on the Wannon River south-west of the Grampians, with a viewing platform.

facts.claim: Punchbowl waterfall on the Wannon River, about 19-20 km west of Hamilton
Formed by a basalt lava flow; drops into a deep plunge pool
A cantilevered viewing platform gives views of the falls; best after rain
Reserve has a rotunda with geology and history displays, picnic and barbecue facilities and a free overnight campground

access_note: Flow depends on rain; can be a trickle in dry summers

name: Mount Rouse
bio_draft: Volcanic peak near Penshurst with a summit walk and views over the volcanic plains.

facts.claim: Extinct volcano next to Penshurst, 367 m high and 145 m above the volcanic plain
Protected as the Mount Rouse and Crater Reserve
Crater lake and a walking track down to the crater off the Mount Rouse Tourist Road
Summit viewing platform has 360-degree views to the Grampians and over farmland

name: Mount Arapiles
bio_draft: Mount Arapiles-Tooan State Park: world-class rock climbing cliffs, with walks and views over the Wimmera.

facts.claim: Mount Arapiles-Tooan State Park covers 7,475 ha in the Wimmera and includes Mount Arapiles, Mitre Rock and the Tooan block
Dyurrite rises abruptly from the flat Wimmera Plain with panoramic views; 334 km north-west of Melbourne, near Natimuk
Walks: 15 km Circuit Walk, 4 km Gully Loop and a 1 km summit nature walk with spring wildflowers
Well-known rock climbing area; about 14% of Victoria's plant species are found here

access_note: New access arrangements (Dyurrite Cultural Landscape) take effect from October 2026: some climbing routes closed or re-routed, some areas restricted

name: Pink Lake Dimboola
bio_draft: Salt lake near Dimboola that turns pink in dry conditions.

facts.claim: Small salt lake about 6 km north-west of Dimboola along the Western Highway.
Colour comes from a salt-tolerant alga in the salt crust and is most striking after rain; it can fade to white in extended dry heat.
A parking area is a short walk from the lake's edge.

access_note: Colour varies with season and rain; can look white when dry.

name: The Stick Shed
bio_draft: Giant 1940s timber grain store at Murtoa, one of the largest of its kind, open to visitors.

facts.claim: Murtoa No. 1 Grain Store, built Sept 1941 to Jan 1942 as an emergency wheat store; the only remaining shed of its type in Australia.
Its cathedral-like interior has 560 unmilled mountain ash poles; it is on the National Heritage List.
The shed is 270 m long and 60 m wide.

name: Murtoa Silo Art
bio_draft: Silo mural at Murtoa on the Wimmera silo art trail, a short roadside stop.

facts.claim: Silo mural by SMUG on the Wimmera Mallee Silo Art Trail.
It celebrates Murtoa's link to Dr John Cade, who discovered the effect of lithium on mental illness.

name: Rupanyup Silo Art
bio_draft: Silo mural at Rupanyup on the Wimmera silo art trail, a short roadside stop.

facts.claim: Silo mural by Russian artist Julia Volchkova on the Silo Art Trail.
It shows the town's young people and their love of team sport (the Rupanyup Panthers football and netball club).

name: Arkona Silo Art
bio_draft: Silo mural at Arkona on the Wimmera silo art trail, a short roadside stop.

facts.claim: Silo mural about 10 km north of Dimboola on the Dimboola-Rainbow Road.
It features local man Roley Klinge and highlights the importance of country tennis to small towns.

name: Little Desert National Park
bio_draft: Large sand-dune heath wilderness south of Nhill, with walks, wildflowers and birds.

facts.claim: 132,647-hectare national park in the Wimmera Mallee, near Dimboola, about 375 km west of Melbourne.
Marked walks range from 30 minutes to three days; camping at Ackle Bend, Horseshoe Bend and Kiata.
Best from late winter to early summer, when wildflowers are in bloom; birdwatching along the Wimmera River.

access_note: Eastern Block closed after the January 2025 bushfire (70% of park burnt); staged re-opening under way, some areas still closed.
